detailed_description: The HTML Preview tool lets you edit HTML and view the rendered result in an iframe-style preview area. The page starts with a sample document, refreshes the preview when requested, and includes a clear action for starting over. It is useful for testing small HTML snippets, learning markup structure, or checking quick layout ideas. The preview is not a full browser development environment: it does not bundle assets, run a build step, or replace cross-browser testing for production pages.
usage_steps: Edit the sample HTML or paste your own snippet.
Click Refresh Preview when you want to reload the rendered result.
Inspect the preview area to see how the markup appears.
Adjust the HTML and refresh again as needed.
Use Clear to empty the editor.
Move production code into a real project and test it there before publishing.
usage_examples: Preview a small HTML card before adding it to documentation.
Test a heading, paragraph, and link structure while learning HTML.
Check an embed snippet quickly without creating a new file.
Clear the editor and start a new sample from scratch.

faqs.question: Does the preview update automatically?
faqs.answer: The page includes a refresh action so you can reload the preview after editing.

faqs.question: Can I test complete websites here?
faqs.answer: It is best for snippets and small examples, not complete production websites.

faqs.question: Does it run a build process?
faqs.answer: No. It previews the HTML you provide directly in the page.

faqs.question: Can I clear the editor?
faqs.answer: Yes. Use the Clear action to empty the HTML input.

faqs.question: Should I still test in real browsers?
faqs.answer: Yes. Use real browser testing for production pages, responsive behavior, and external assets.
